releases.name: v0.16.11 — Advisor per-request consultation scope
releases.body:
# v0.16.11 — Advisor per-request consultation scope

## Changes

- Clarify that each host-admitted Strategy request covers one candidate and one focused question, not a reused Advisor session's entire lifetime. A previous answer alone does not consume an invented consultation slot or require a fresh Advisor session.
- Evaluate the current admitted question, new evidence and explicit corrections; earlier advice is context, not authority over current constraints. Preserve existing host admission, duplicate/retry controls, explicit budgets, tool-free advice, no implementation and no SourceReview. Advice grants no execution, retry, scope or budget authority and is not validation or acceptance.
- The canonical Advisor body renders into the Mission profile. No consultation helper/config API, host counter, model default, permission, Mission state, dependency or budget change. Only package/runtime identity advances for this release.

## Investigation and bounded evidence

The user's screenshot was traced to a saved native Advisor history: the host delivered a second distinct question with new observations, but the actual `openai/gpt-6-astra#xhigh` Advisor refused because it had previously answered one Strategy request. This was a model-visible refusal, not evidence of a host quota denial. The exact historical assembled provider request was not captured; the wording is not claimed as its sole historical cause.

The requested authenticated ChatGPT browser consultation recommended a local wording fix rather than disposable Advisor sessions, new IDs/counters or public helper/config changes. Only public source snippets and anonymized facts were shared. See `docs/investigations/advisor-request-boundary-20261106.md`.

A controlled native CLI rendering probe used the same actual Astra/xhigh model and two synthetic questions per retained primary-mode session. The old body refused the second question; the new body returned two concrete explanations and one recommendation about the new runtime/checker observations while preserving unmeasured performance. Four replies, no tools or child sessions: **139.622 seconds / $0.180396 / zero unpriced requests**. This is a primary-mode adaptation of the rendered body, not native Coordinator/Advisor child Task integration, original GPU-task recovery, official scoring, universal compliance or a speed/quality comparison. Browser/author billing is unmeasured, not zero.

Before the fix, new contract/profile checks produced 152 passes / 2 expected failures. After the fix, related Fast-lane, packed-loader, V010-runtime and Mission-completion checks passed **204/204**, exit 0, 23.143 seconds. Same-trigger/candidate/reused-child admission is covered alongside unchanged duplicate, unauthorized/exhausted fallback and invalid-trigger denials.

The already-running feature full completed with **2,547 PASS / 4 skip**, 134 files, exit 0, 421.935 seconds. Release-profile identity checks then passed **4/4**, 8.401 seconds. These are retained source/preparation observations, not a substitute for final integrated candidate gates.

## Release boundary

The user subsequently requested the release routine. Integrate the reviewed fix/release PR, pin one main commit and archive/SHA-256, run packed preflight, the mandatory final-commit full suite and actual final-archive Worker/model startup, then globally install, tag, attach and publish that same archive once. A feature full suite was already underway when the request expanded; retain its evidence separately instead of treating it as the final release-identity gate. Do not replay the completed Advisor comparison or the original private workload merely for release.

Reuse the proven short physical tmpfs and the previously diagnosed active-credential selector only in copied isolated verification tooling. releases.name: v0.16.10 — Useful early parallel Scout discovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.10 — Useful early parallel Scout discovery

## Changes

- Restore early, concrete repository discovery instead of waiting for a proven blocking evidence gap. Fast-first Operator, Mission Coordinator and canonical routing share one policy: zero Scouts when existing evidence or direct work is sufficient, one for one useful question, and two or three independent useful questions in one parallel foreground round. No mandatory-three ritual, extra Coordinator or preparation unit.
- Scout uses native Read/Glob/Grep to follow relevant callers and tests. Known paths become seeds/search areas rather than a four-path read allowlist. Remove the 120-line, one-read-per-path and 800-character instruction limits; retain eight steps, Luna Fast max, existing question codes/four JSON keys and native host permissions. Shell/web/edits/child dispatch remain outside Scout.
- Reuse source path/line facts and unresolved risks in the next Worker's objective/handoff context. Required author source inspection and validation freshness remain legitimate. Discovery is not validation, independent Review or acceptance.
- Early root Scouts now use the existing Mission consultation recording/model/outcome/result/reload path even before an implementation run exists. Existing Reviewer generated-task/source checks, Advisor routing, execution grants, Worker budget and formal root acceptance remain unchanged.

## Source evidence and limits

PR #335 includes the user-requested completed ChatGPT browser consultation and adoption/source checks in `docs/investigations/scout-initial-discovery-20261106.md`. Existing PR body/submitted/ordinary/inline reviews are collected before integration and publication; CI is not finding resolution. No original private task, session, DB, ledger, model or budget was modified or replayed.

The fixed source pilot demonstrated three actual Luna Fast max Scouts dispatched in the same foreground tool round, discovery beyond the two seed files and decisive lines beyond 120, useful source facts/uncertainty in the actual Worker handoff, one Terra max Worker fix, passing public check, independent fixture Reviewer PASS and formal acceptance. Native CLI elapsed 303.105 seconds; estimated priced usage $0.30676588, zero unpriced requests. One root-model Task-reference transcription was correctly rejected and repaired in the same unit before Worker launch; it is retained rather than hidden.

The pilot explicitly requested the discovery route and had substantial overlap between Scout reads. It does not prove autonomous default utilization, causal speed/cost savings or matched quality superiority. No official/hidden benchmark score is claimed. Browser/author billing is unmeasured, not zero. The completed source pilot is reused rather than replayed solely for this release.

## Release verification boundary

Fix an integrated main commit and one archive/SHA-256, perform packed preflight, one mandatory full suite, same-commit CI and actual Worker/model startup, then apply/attach/publish the same archive once. Final source verification was 285 targeted passes and 2,545 full passes/4 platform skips; final package/main results are recorded separately, not inferred from those earlier receipts.

Use the proven short physical tmpfs environment and the already-diagnosed active-credential selection only in copied isolated verification tooling; shared authentication and production helper source are unchanged. Preserve explicit models and unrelated global/project configuration across global installation and asset initialization. Do not restart the shared OpenCode service automatically. Installed archive/asset identity is separate from loaded identity in a running host.

Release evidence: `_testenv/releases/0.16.10/`. Source/pilot evidence: `_testenv/investigations/20261106-scout-discovery/`.

releases.name: v0.16.9 — Active Mission terminal policy
releases.body:
# v0.16.9 — Keep one-shot terminal instructions out of active Missions

## Fix

An Advisor admission could arm the shared core's one-shot terminal instruction before any implementation unit or Worker existed. Forwarding that instruction during an active Mission contradicted its retained multi-step requirements and formal acceptance lifecycle.

The profiled system transform now removes only its generated `SORTIE_FAST_LANE_TERMINAL` block while the durable Mission is neither completed nor cancelled, including a stale supplied copy. The existing V2 live-state mechanism withdraws a previously sent block. Genuine one-shot mode remains available outside the active Mission; its default is explicitly not evidence that the user requested a one-unit limit.

No execution/consultation budget, Worker limit, acceptance/validation, compaction capability, parent/child rule or dispatch permission changes. No extra approval, new monitor, schema migration or configuration option. Actual stops must still be judged from the original user request, current host state and native results rather than an assumed user restriction.

## Verification and limits

- Public-hook regressions cover open/running/submitted and completed/cancelled state, advice before a run or Worker exists, root/nested-Coordinator admission, plugin recreation, stale live-state withdrawal and unchanged requests/ownership/Goal/budget/receipt records.
- Related Fast-lane, Fast-first, live-state and V2 tests: 129 passed, exit 0, 12.171 seconds. Focused shared-core one-shot/backlog regressions: exit 0, 10.014 seconds. Final integrated release gates are recorded separately.
- Saved V2 history confirms the reported helper diagnostic and an Advisor reuse rejected by native parent/child ownership. That rejection is valid and not bypassed. The exact historical model request containing the one-shot block was not captured; this correction is not proof that the block alone caused the overnight pause, or that the original work has resumed or completed.
- Investigation: `docs/investigations/mission-one-shot-terminal-20261106.md`. Original work, private artifacts, sessions, DBs, ledgers, cumulative spend and settings are not changed by the investigation/release.

## Release boundary

Fix one integrated main commit and one archive/SHA-256 before packed preflight, one mandatory full suite, same-commit CI and actual Worker/model startup. Reuse the proven short physical tmpfs layout from v0.16.8 to avoid its archive-backed short-TTL fixture failure; do not alter test timing or production logic. Apply, attach and publish the same archive once, preserving explicit models and unrelated configuration. No automatic shared-service restart or original-task replay.

Evidence: `_testenv/investigations/20261106-mission-terminal-instruction/` and `_testenv/releases/0.16.9/`. Installed artifacts are distinct from the code loaded by a running shared host; startup is not instruction completion or official benchmark scoring.

releases.name: v0.16.8 — Queued goal registration with retained spend
releases.body:
# v0.16.8 — Register queued requests without reopening terminal goals or resetting spend

## Included changes

- Integrates PR #332, source head `43e61ccb291d74702dbdc7697eba359952417c99`. A separately queued real user request received before Goal A finished can now register as Goal B after A's formal success, rather than attempting an invalid revision of A's terminal state.
- A limited `goal.queued-accepted` event binds the exact settled predecessor receipt, unchanged budget, current Mission and unused native request. The normal root/user-message/content/timing checks and pinned prepared-run controls remain in force. Ordinary new-goal acceptance remains a separate budget lineage.
- Consumption of units, time, cost and validation budget is derived from the prior state. For example, 28 consumed units out of 32 remain 28/32, not 0/32. A's receipt, original records, attachments, failures and evidence remain unchanged; A's passing evidence is not B's acceptance proof.
- An interruption after acceptance or before Mission/run binding reuses the same prepared run. Late native usage from A can reconcile once into the shared queued budget using the exact goal/reservation/native-session identity, without rewriting A's receipt or accepting another request.
- Existing ledger formats, immutable blob storage, locking/hash chain, normal scope revision, current writer protection, cancelled-direct-writer release, compact background notifications and history/debrief callers remain supported. Older reducers reject the new cross-goal event instead of silently resetting consumption; use this compatible runtime for histories containing it.

## Source evidence and review

- Saved V2 history identified the terminal-revision refusal followed by `mission-run-registration-incomplete`; it was not evidence of exhausted unit budget or an image-compression failure.
- The author reports actual ChatGPT browser consultation and its adopted/rejected advice in `docs/investigations/queued-terminal-goal-registration-20261105.md`. Advice is not execution authority or formal validation.
- Author's final targeted run: 169 passed, two skipped, exit 0, 99.604 seconds. Full: 133 files, exit 0, 420.947 seconds. Native Windows: 19 passed, 19.871 seconds. Fixtures cover root/Coordinator paths, crash/reload reuse, retained receipts/spend, invalid or repeated requests, limits, writer conflicts and late usage accounting.
- The independent reviewer's Medium late-usage finding was corrected by that reviewer, followed by formal checks and author self-recheck. This is not a post-correction independent PASS. Existing PR body, submitted reviews and ordinary/inline comments were collected before integration. Cloud review failed at its usage quota without a concrete source finding; its machine flags are not treated as code findings, and no cloud Review PASS is claimed. CI is separate from finding resolution.

## Release boundary

Fix one integrated `main` commit and one `.tgz`/SHA-256 before isolated candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite, same-commit CI and actual Worker/model startup. Apply, attach and publish that same archive once. Preserve explicit model choices, unrelated configuration and live sessions; no automatic shared-service restart.

The original real request, private images/site/DB/ledger and cumulative budget are not modified or resumed by this release. Packed startup is not proof of that live task's recovery, completed instructions or an official benchmark score. The already-running host's loaded version remains separate from installed package verification.

Evidence: `_testenv/releases/0.16.8/`.

## Verified candidate

releases.name: v0.16.7 — Cancelled direct writer recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.7 — Release cancelled direct writers from native terminal records

## Fix

A cancelled direct Coordinator could retain its write authorization when a tool's `execute.after` hook was missed. Cancellation had already stopped the owned child and settled its reservation, but `releaseDirectUnit` returned `tools-in-flight`. A replacement Mission then encountered `mission-scope-update-writer-conflict`; redispatching the old Coordinator correctly failed ownership authorization and could not repair it.

Direct release now reuses the existing exact-call native-history reconciliation. Each pending call must have one completed/error tool record in that actor's history; foreign, duplicate, missing, running/pending or background-unknown records retain the writer. Calls admitted while history is loading are not erased by a blanket clear.

If release still cannot complete, its exact authorization identity is retained in memory. The next ordinary bind/scope-expansion operation under the same root retries that requested release before checking overlap. Changed authorizations are not released. No old-Coordinator redispatch, new watcher, user approval, persistent-state migration, raw ledger mutation, budget reset or forced eviction is introduced. A pending cancellation still reports its actual release failure; a later native terminal can resolve the writer without another model dispatch.

## Regression and boundaries

- Public plugin-hook fixtures reproduce missing `execute.after`, stale question activity, delayed terminal, background unknown, missing/duplicate/foreign tool records and repeated/concurrent scope operations.
- The replacement scope succeeds only after native termination is established. Old-Coordinator redispatch stays denied; cancelled reservations are not settled twice and only the replacement direct unit holds new budget.
- Source investigation used saved V2 history read-only. The original product Mission, private artifacts and cumulative spend were not modified or resumed; fixing the harness is not proof of that product's completion.
- Actual ChatGPT browser consultation recommended lazy recovery using the existing native-terminal verifier rather than a new monitor. Consultation is advice, not independent source review or formal PASS.

## Release

Fix one integrated `main` commit and archive/SHA-256, run isolated candidate preflight and the mandatory full suite, verify actual Worker/model startup, then globally apply, tag, create the GitHub Release and publish that same archive once. Preserve explicit model choices and unrelated configuration. Do not restart the shared OpenCode service automatically.

Evidence: `_testenv/investigations/20261105-mission-dispatch-recovery/` and `_testenv/releases/0.16.7/`. Startup verification is not a completed Mission or official benchmark score.
